issues.description: Weak email validation regex doesn't comply with RFC 5322. The pattern `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` allows invalid emails like `a@b.c` and doesn't properly validate TLDs.
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation approach. Either use a well-tested library like `email-validator` or implement RFC 5322 compliant validation. For basic validation, consider: `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}$/` with additional domain validation.

issues.description: Email field is not sanitized before storage, only the name is. If the email is ever rendered in HTML context without encoding, it could be a potential XSS vector.
issues.suggestion: Apply sanitization to the email field as well: `email: sanitizeInput(input.email.toLowerCase())`

issues.description: ID generation using `Math.random()` is not cryptographically secure and could be predictable. This is problematic if IDs are exposed and used for security purposes or authorization checks.
issues.suggestion: Use cryptographically secure random generation: `import { randomBytes } from 'crypto'; return 'user_' + randomBytes(16).toString('hex');` or use a UUID library.

issues.description: Email regex is compiled every time `isValidEmail()` is called, creating unnecessary object allocations. This impacts performance if the function is called frequently.
issues.suggestion: Move the regex outside the function as a constant: `const EMAIL_REGEX = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;`

issues.description: Using 4 sequential `.replace()` calls creates 4 intermediate strings. While minor, this could be optimized for better performance on high-volume input processing.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a single regex with replacement: `input.replace(/[<>"']/g, (char) => ({...}[char] || char));`

issues.description: Hardcoded database query in function. If schema changes or the query needs to be modified, it must be updated here. No abstraction layer exists.
issues.suggestion: Consider moving queries to a constants file or database abstraction layer: `const USER_INSERT_QUERY = 'INSERT INTO users...`

issues.description: The `saveUser()` function has no error handling. If the database query fails, the error will propagate without context, making debugging difficult.
issues.suggestion: In production code, add error handling: `try { await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Failed to save user: ${error.message}`); }`

issues.description: No validation on input length/size for `email` or `name`. Extremely long inputs could cause database issues or buffer problems.
issues.suggestion: Add length constraints: `const MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH = 254;` and `const MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 255;` with validation checks.

issues.description: Throwing generic `Error` objects instead of custom error types makes error handling less specific and harder to test.
issues.suggestion: Create custom error classes: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; } }`

recommendations.description: Create comprehensive test suite with 40+ test cases for fixtures/clean-code.ts. The file has zero test coverage and contains critical security-sensitive functions (email validation, XSS sanitization). Priority test areas: email validation (13 tests), input sanitization (11 tests), user creation workflow (12 tests), and ID generation (3 tests).

Improve email validation using RFC 5322 compliant validation or a well-tested library. Current regex allows invalid formats like 'a@b.c'. Consider using email-validator library or stronger regex pattern like `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}$/`.
Extract validation logic from createUser() into dedicated validateCreateUserInput() function. This improves separation of concerns, testability, and allows reuse of validation logic elsewhere.

Optimize sanitizeInput() function by replacing four sequential .replace() calls with a single regex pass using character map. This improves performance on high-volume input processing while maintaining readability.

Replace Math.random()-based ID generation with cryptographically secure approach. Consider using UUID library (v4) or crypto.randomBytes() to ensure IDs cannot be predicted, especially important if used for security/authorization.
Apply HTML sanitization to email field in addition to name field. While email is validated, if ever rendered in HTML context without encoding, it could be a potential XSS vector.
Extract email regex pattern to named constant (EMAIL_PATTERN). This creates single source of truth for validation, improves performance by avoiding regex recompilation, and makes intent clearer.
Add error handling wrapper around saveUser() call in createUser(). This provides better error context, prevents unhandled rejections, and makes debugging easier.
Modernize ID generation by using UUID library instead of custom Date.now() + Math.random() approach. This provides industry-standard, collision-free identifiers.
Add input length validation for email and name fields. Set MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH=254 (RFC 5321) and MAX_NAME_LENGTH=255 to prevent extremely long inputs from causing database or buffer issues.
Replace generic Error objects with custom error types (e.g., ValidationError). This makes error handling more specific, improves testability, and provides better error context.
Extract hardcoded SQL query to named constant or move to database abstraction layer. This centralizes query management and makes schema changes easier to track.
Add JSDoc comment to saveUser() clarifying parameter order mapping ($1=id, $2=email, $3=name, $4=created_at). This prevents parameter ordering mistakes in future updates.
